kyle: heads-up: saw weird KV cache behavior during long-context mlperf-ish runs on mi250x. memory keeps creeping even tho eviction rate looks normal. paging spikes after ~1.8M tokens.
mai: can you share traces? is this the same reuse-window regression from last month?
kyle: different. reusable entries are not being reclaimed because page table entries end up fragmented into many tiny pages. eviction churn goes up and we see repeated pagewalk stalls. attached trace: `ciara-bot` uploaded perf trace link: https://ciara.internal/runs/3105556667/trace.vz
ciara-bot: perf-trace: https://ciara.internal/runs/3105556667/trace.vz (auto-upload)
olivia: repro steps? hw + driver?
kyle: repro on h100 and mi250x, both with the new tiled-kernel selector. Ubuntu 22.04, cuda 12.1 on H100, ROCm 5.9 on MI250X. command used: `./tools/run_longctx.sh --model small --tokens 2000000 --batch 8`
ryan: outputs? any OOMs or just slowdowns?
kyle: no OOM, just slow token p99 and VRAM growth ~200MB over baseline by 1.8M tokens. CPU-side we see many PT-walk retries in the kernel logs:```[kv_pager] evict: slot 0x3f7 owner mismatch, retrying
[ptwalk] walk_latency_us=1200 (expected < 200)
[kv_cache] reuse_window_misses=3421
```
mai: logs look like repeated evict failures. could be ABA/reuse-window delta. did you capture kvcache telemetry?
kyle: yes, telemetry attached in the trace. interestingly h100 shows more regular coalesced pages but mi250x ends up with highly fragmented slotmap -> many tiny allocations. suspect allocator alignment + PCIe atomics timing.
olivia: any kernel selection differences? tiled kernels do different per-arch allocation patterns.
kyle: yep. the tiled kernel path uses a different per-thread allocation granularity for page entries. on h100 that lines up with 256B boundaries; on mi250x the backend allocator rounds differently (64B) causing more small fragments.
ryan: can we try forcing the fallback kernel (linear) to see if that stabilizes reuse?
kyle: did that locally: fallback removes the slow growth but p50 latency increases ~8%. Not ideal but helps prove kernel selection is a factor.
mai: next steps: 1) capture per-alloc alignment + slotmap fragmentation histogram, 2) add a short-term compensating coalesce pass during eviction to merge adjacent tiny spans, 3) produce a small reproducible case for CI.
olivia: how invasive is coalesce pass? might be okay as a hotfix. we need to be careful with concurrency.
kyle: prototype patch:```diff
--- a/runtime/kvcache/pager.cpp
+++ b/runtime/kvcache/pager.cpp
@@
- evict_span(span_t s) { free(s); }
+ evict_span(span_t s) { coalesce_if_adjacent(s); free(s); }
```
mai: can you add debug telemetry to measure coalesce effectiveness (bytes reclaimed, merge count) and toggle with env var `KVCOALESCE=1`?
kyle: already added local env toggle, results: with coalesce on mi250x growth drops by ~75% in 500k token window, reuse-window misses down 60%.
ryan: nice. any regressions on h100?
kyle: none observed in short runs. small p1 tail increase but within noise.
mai: let's not land yet. need stress runs and cross-arch CI. also check interaction with prefix caching and batching heuristics (larger batches make reuse window wider).
olivia: also add a diagnostic dump when fragmentation crosses threshold: slotmap layout + page ranges so we can postmortem future incidents.
kyle: noted. I'll push a WIP patch and attach perf traces. linking WIP: https://phabricator.internal/D12345
ciara-bot: buildkite: started job #3624 for D12345 (kyle)
mai: assign to me to drive cross-arch runs. @olivia please eyeball concurrency safety. @ryan can you add the CI job with ROCm matrix?
ryan: on it. will add a nightly with mi250x and h100 combos.
olivia: if coalescing fixes it, we should backport to 1.8.x as a mitigation and follow up with kernel selector tuning.
kyle: agree. I'll also add a reproducer that toggles kernel selection so CI can catch regressions earlier.
mai: great. for tracking, create an incident-ish ticket and attach the traces + the small repro. set priority P2 for now.
ryan: adding tests: microbench that simulates long-context eviction pattern with deterministic RNG.
kyle: thanks y'all. I'll update the phab with logs and a binary artifact for bench runs.
mai: thanks. ping if you need GPUs for stress. :thumbsup:
